6	# Agents.md rule bundles
7	
8	## Goal
9	A person using the agent today gets one fixed set of rules: the ones that make the agent work the way it does, and beside them matters of taste and practice — reproduce a bug before fixing it, refactor towards SOLID, name things this way — that not every team wants and no team can decline. Rule bundles separate the two. A bundle is a named, versioned set of rule text kept in a git repository, applied into the workspace's or the person's `AGENTS.md`, where both engines already read it and the whole team can see it in their source. The product keeps its own catalog, so anyone contributes a bundle by a pull request against it, and a company points the agent at its own repositories and names there the bundles its teams must carry. Because the rules now live in `AGENTS.md`, a workspace still on `CLAUDE.md` is offered, once, to move.
10	
11	## Rules that became optional
12	What the agent guarantees about itself and what the person chooses are no longer the same list.
13	- **Core behaviour stays in the prompt**: the rules that make a phase what it is — the planner's blindness to the code, the spec contract, reading before writing, tests as the evidence of done — are the agent's own instructions and no bundle can remove, replace or override them (docs/intent/agent.md#Instructions).
14	- **Optional mechanics ship as bundles**: the judgment rules that are a matter of practice rather than of the agent working at all are gone from every phase's instructions and reach a session only as an applied bundle (docs/intent/agent.md#Instructions).
15	- **Not pre-applied on upgrade**: a workspace in use before bundles existed has none applied for it, so a rule that used to hold by default holds again only once the person has chosen it.
16	- **Bundle rules reach a session as the person's own instructions do**: an applied bundle joins the instructions of a chat session, a plan session, the check against the code and every implementation, testing and cleanup run, exactly where the workspace's and the person's instruction files join them, on either engine (docs/settings.md#Instruction files and skills).
17	  - **Person-scope bundle on either engine**: a bundle applied for the person reaches a session on either engine, the same as one applied for the project.
18	  - **Clash with a core rule**: where a bundle rule contradicts a core rule, the core rule holds and the session says which bundle rule it set aside.
19	  - **No bundles for the blind planner**: a feature-planning session carries no bundle rules, since bundles describe how code is written (docs/intent/agent.md#Skills).
20	
21	## Picking up bundles for a workspace
22	The person has a workspace with no bundles applied, and the agent offers what fits it.
23	- **Suggested once per workspace**: a workspace with no bundle applied draws one offer of the bundles that match it, and dismissing that offer ends it until the person asks for bundles themselves.
24	- **Matched by what the workspace holds**: a bundle declares what it applies to — nothing in particular, a language, or a framework — and only the matching ones are suggested, with the ones that apply to nothing in particular always among them.
25	- **Text seen before it is applied**: the rules a bundle would add are shown before it is applied for the first time, and nothing is written to a file without the person accepting it.
26	- **Project or person scope**: a bundle is applied either for the project, in the workspace's `AGENTS.md`, or for the person, in the `AGENTS.md` of their user profile, and never into a `CLAUDE.md` (docs/settings.md#Instruction files and skills).
27	- **One marked block per bundle**: an applied bundle occupies one block of the file naming its source, its name and its version, and applying, updating or removing a bundle changes nothing outside that block.
28	- **Managed at any time**: the person can see which bundles are available and which are applied, apply one and remove one, without waiting for a suggestion.
29	
30	## Where bundles come from
31	A bundle is fetched from a git repository, the product's own or a company's.
32	- **The product's catalog is a source without being configured**: the product's own bundle repository is always among the sources and is an ordinary git source, so a bundle is contributed by a pull request against it.
33	- **Further sources are git repositories named in settings**: more sources are named as git repository URLs in the person's settings and in the workspace's, the workspace's adding to the person's rather than replacing them.
34	- **Fetched with the git access the person already has**: a source is read with the person's existing git credentials, so a company's private repository needs no sign-in of its own.
35	- **A source is accepted before it is fetched**: a source the person has not accepted before is not fetched until they accept it, named by its repository.
36	  - **Source that arrived with the workspace**: a source named by a workspace the person just cloned is put to them in that workspace like any other new source.
37	- **Unreachable source falls back to the last fetch**: when a source cannot be reached its bundles are offered from the copy last fetched, said to be as of that fetch, and a source never fetched offers nothing.
38	- **Rule text only**: a bundle contributes rule text and nothing else — no commands, tools, permissions or settings — and anything else carried in it is ignored.
39	- **A source may require bundles**: a source repository can name bundles as required, and those are applied for the project the first time that source is used in a workspace.
40	  - **A required bundle comes back**: a required bundle whose block has been removed is applied again, with a line naming the source that requires it.
41	- **Updates are never silent**: when a source holds a newer version of an applied bundle the change is put to the person, and the answer is remembered for that bundle — later versions arrive with a notice, or this version is kept and not raised again until the person asks.
42	  - **Block changed by hand**: when the block of an applied bundle has been edited by hand, that is said before an update replaces it.
43	
44	## Moving from CLAUDE.md to AGENTS.md
45	A workspace or a person whose rules still sit in `CLAUDE.md`.
46	- **Offered once per file**: the move is offered once for the workspace's `CLAUDE.md` and once for the person's own, and a declined offer is not raised again (docs/settings.md#Instruction files and skills).
47	- **Content moves whole**: Accepting the move carries everything the file holds, the person's memories among it, and from then on memories are written to and read from `AGENTS.md`.
48	  - **Confirmed before the file goes**: the move is shown as a change the person confirms before it is made, and `CLAUDE.md` is removed once it is.
49	  - **Both files already there**: when `AGENTS.md` already exists its text is left as it was and the `CLAUDE.md` text is appended under a heading saying where it came from.
50	- **Same rules on both engines after the move**: once moved, a session on either engine works from the one `AGENTS.md` and no rule that reached it before the move stops reaching it (docs/settings.md#Instruction files and skills).

1	import { permissionResolved, type CodeSession, type PermissionDecision, type SessionEvent } from './code-session'
2	import type { ModelProfile, Step } from './model-profile'
3	import type { RunLog } from '../runs/run-log'
4	import { answerText, UNANSWERED_RESULT, type QuestionOutcome, type UserQuestionRequest } from './user-question'
5	import { nextStatus, underWay, type SessionStatus } from './session-status'
6	
7	/**
8	 * `plan` writes a feature's spec blind, `reconcile` checks it against the code
9	 * (together: feature planning), `implement` builds the approved spec, `cleanup`
10	 * splits what the implementation left oversized. `code-plan` agrees on intent
11	 * and then plans against the code, with no spec, and is built in the same
12	 * session once the plan is approved. `docs` judges how the docs a blind planner reads are
13	 * arranged, `docs-map` describes them so it can find its way, and
14	 * `file-decisions` files the user's unfiled decisions into the specs and docs;
15	 * none of those belongs to a feature.
16	 */
17	export type SessionMode = 'chat' | 'plan' | 'reconcile' | 'implement' | 'cleanup' | 'code-plan' | 'docs' | 'docs-map' | 'file-decisions'
18	
19	/** Planning rather than building: no blanket allow for writes. */
20	export const isPlanning = (mode: Step): boolean =>
21	  mode === 'plan' || mode === 'reconcile' || mode === 'code-plan' || mode === 'docs' || mode === 'file-decisions'
22	
23	/**
24	 * The steps a profile names a model for, in the order the settings page lists
25	 * them. A step is a mode: what a session is for is what decides how strong a
26	 * model it earns, so there is no second vocabulary to keep in step.
27	 */
28	export const STEPS: { step: Step; label: string; hint: string }[] = [
29	  { step: 'chat', label: 'Chat', hint: 'Work in the code with the full tool set.' },
30	  { step: 'plan', label: 'Feature planning', hint: 'Write the spec from the intent docs, blind to the code.' },
31	  { step: 'code-plan', label: 'Plan', hint: 'Agree on intent, then plan against the code.' },
32	  { step: 'reconcile', label: 'Check against code', hint: 'Name each disagreement between the approved spec and the code before it is built.' },
33	  { step: 'implement', label: 'Implement', hint: 'Build the approved spec, task by task, with a test per rule.' },
34	  { step: 'fix', label: 'Fix', hint: 'Mend what a failed test run names; one effort level harder each time it fails again.' },
35	  { step: 'cleanup', label: 'Cleanup', hint: 'Split what the implementation left oversized.' },
36	  { step: 'docs', label: 'Evaluate docs', hint: 'Judge how the docs a blind planner reads are arranged.' },
37	  { step: 'docs-map', label: 'Docs map', hint: 'Describe the docs so a blind planner can find its way.' },
38	  { step: 'file-decisions', label: 'File decisions', hint: "File the user's unfiled decisions into the specs and docs they belong in." },
39	]
40	
41	/** The modes that stand on their own rather than on a feature's plan files. */
42	export const isFeatureless = (mode: Step): boolean =>
43	  mode === 'chat' || mode === 'code-plan' || mode === 'docs' || mode === 'docs-map' || mode === 'file-decisions'
44	
45	/** A build, not a conversation: it has no tab and no entry of its own, and nobody prompts it. */
46	export const isBuild = (mode: SessionMode): boolean => mode === 'docs-map'
47	
48	export type SessionRecord = {
49	  id: string
50	  title: string
51	  profile: ModelProfile
52	  mode: SessionMode
53	  /** The feature whose spec the session works on; every mode but chat. */
54	  feature?: string
55	  /** The session whose tab this one runs under: a check runs under its plan session and never gets a tab of its own. */
56	  parentId?: string
57	  /** The workspace-relative paths a run was handed: what a cleanup may write, what a docs map build may read. */
58	  files?: string[]
59	  /** The board task an implement run builds; absent on a run that fixes a failed test sweep. */
60	  task?: string
